list.item: Tobacco use disorder, severe: about twenty cigars a day for about fifty years, with many failed attempts to stop; synthetic modern episode linked to his documented cigar smoking: active, confirmed [S]

Squamous cell carcinoma of the right hard and soft palate seven years ago, treated by right partial maxillectomy with clear margins (pT2 N0) and no radiation in this synthetic history, with no recurrence on yearly surveillance: active, confirmed [S]
Acquired defect of the right maxilla and palate after maxillectomy, closed with an obturator prosthesis that is now worn and fits poorly: active, confirmed [S]
Hypernasal speech and nasal leakage of liquids from a poorly sealing obturator: active, confirmed [S]
Chronic pain at the maxillectomy site and right cheek, worse where the obturator rubs: active, confirmed [S]
Raised LDL cholesterol (126 mg/dL) with a high estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk after fifty years of smoking: active, confirmed [S]
Weight loss of 4 kg in six months from painful chewing and leakage, with a low albumin: active, confirmed [S]

Tobacco: a nonjudgmental assessment of readiness and of what cigars do for him; varenicline started now, before a quit date, with a plan to cut down and then stop; combination nicotine replacement (patch and lozenge) added from the quit date; cigars are counted like any other tobacco; weekly behavioral support by phone with the national quitline and in clinic; relapse treated as part of the process. Guideline: Initiating Pharmacologic Treatment in Tobacco-Dependent Adults. An Official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline (2020); Tobacco Smoking Cessation in Adults, Including Pregnant Persons: Interventions (2021) [S]

Maxillofacial prosthodontics consultation for a worn, poorly sealing obturator with pain, hypernasal speech and nasal leakage, and for dental care. Guideline: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Head and Neck Cancers, Version 2.2026 (follow-up and survivorship) (2026); American Cancer Society Head and Neck Cancer Survivorship Care Guideline (2016) [S]

Head and neck cancer survivorship: yearly examination of the mouth, defect and neck by his head and neck surgeon (more than five years after treatment), self-examination of the mouth, prompt review of any sore, lump, bleeding or change that lasts two weeks, imaging only for symptoms, and counseling on the risk of second primary cancers of the mouth, throat, larynx, esophagus and lung, which stopping smoking lowers. Guideline: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Head and Neck Cancers, Version 2.2026 (follow-up and survivorship) (2026); American Cancer Society Head and Neck Cancer Survivorship Care Guideline (2016) [S]

Chronic pain: scheduled acetaminophen up to 3,000 mg a day, a well-fitting obturator, warm saline rinses, and no long-term opioids; the plan is reviewed at each visit with a pain score. Guideline: American Cancer Society Head and Neck Cancer Survivorship Care Guideline (2016); CDC Clinical Practice Guideline for Prescribing Opioids for Pain — United States, 2022 (2022) [S]

Nutrition: dietitian advice on soft high-protein meals, oral nutrition supplements twice daily, weight at each visit and albumin rechecked. Guideline: American Cancer Society Head and Neck Cancer Survivorship Care Guideline (2016) [S]

Cardiovascular risk: lipid panel and 10-year risk estimate; a statin discussed with him once the smoking plan is under way. Guideline: Statin Use for the Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease in Adults: Preventive Medication (2022) [S]
